calculator.title: Engineering input check
calculator.description: Submit rider, bike, tire, rim, and manufacturer source data. The current model is not calibrated and will not return a pressure recommendation.
calculator.limitDescription: Enter a source record. The server does not authenticate the document; it marks the limit as provided and unverified.
calculator.noRecommendation: No pressure recommendation is available until a calibrated model is approved. Follow the exact tire, rim, and wheel manufacturer instructions.
calculator.requestFailed: The engineering check could not be completed.

dashboard.svgLabel: Front and rear tire axial sections, rims, and contact projection
dashboard.svgDescription: Uses simplified axial sections for tire width, air cavity, rim, and axle. The red arrow illustrates horizontal lateral demand; the green double-ended scale shows bidirectional grip capacity, not an actual force direction; the vertical arrow shows vertical load. The tire bottoms meet the level road and rotate with lean. The contact projection is an estimate, not measured data.
dashboard.contactAreaDescription: Area is estimated with A = Fz ÷ P: vertical wheel load divided by operating pressure. It is not measured rubber contact area; lean mainly changes patch position and shape.
dashboard.fixedPressureHint: Fixed pressure isolates how load changes affect the estimated load-bearing area.
dashboard.title: Dynamic tire pressure and cornering grip simulator
dashboard.subtitle: Front/rear load · lean-angle demand · contact patch · impedance diagnostics
dashboard.noticeBody: This dashboard visualizes a provisional physics model. It does not issue a production tire-pressure recommendation. Follow tire, rim, and wheel manufacturer limits.
dashboard.controlBaselineBody: All dynamic simulations in this dashboard concerning cornering lean grip, maximum lateral static friction, and anti-crash safety margin are based on an academic and industrial baseline in which all other external conditions are held strictly identical (including the same high-grip premium silica-compound tire formulation, the same microscopic drainage tread depth and distribution (Tread Pattern/Siping), the same supple 300 TPI casing, and consistent lateral wheel stiffness). In real riding, if the tire is excessively worn and becomes slick, the tread has lost effectiveness, or the road contains loose sand, oil, or leaves, the actual coefficient of friction can deteriorate sharply and the maximum safe lean angle can shrink substantially.
dashboard.contactPatchValue: Estimated load-bearing area {area} cm² · L {length} cm · W {width} cm · {state}
dashboard.scienceTitle: 3. Physics notes: cornering friction and impedance
dashboard.mechanicalBody: Casing deflection and contact area influence the usable friction envelope. This visualization is a model aid, not a measured tire test.
dashboard.riskBody: Excess pressure can reduce casing conformity and cornering margin on imperfect surfaces. Verify limits against the exact tire and rim documents.
dashboard.scopeBody: The current production API returns loads and supplied limits only. No uncalibrated pressure recommendation is presented.
dashboard.diagnosticBody: At {lean}° lean, lateral demand is {front} / {rear} N front/rear. Contact patches are estimated from load, pressure, and casing width.

intro.matching: For safety and performance, the tire and rim on the bike must be perfectly matched. This applies even more to tubeless tires. Alongside classic hooked rims, hookless rims are becoming increasingly popular. Hookless rims place particularly high demands on tubeless tires for safe operation. Schwalbe TLR and TLE models from model year 2020 are designed to meet these requirements, especially around the bead core, and are generally compatible.
intro.width: Rim manufacturers often use wider inner bead widths for hookless rims. Tire pressure should therefore be reduced accordingly because the real tire volume increases with wider inner rim widths.
intro.etrto: Hookless pressure limits depend on the exact rim, wheel, and tire instructions. Check each manufacturer's stated limit and follow the lowest applicable value. Do not assume a universal pressure limit from the rim type alone; manufacturers may also restrict tire choice and minimum tire width.

why.title: 1. Why tire pressure matters
why.performance: Too high means less grip; too low means more rolling resistance.
why.safety: Overinflation can damage rims; underinflation increases the risk of pinch flats.
why.comfort: Correct pressure reduces vibration and improves ride quality.

tireWidth.explanation: Wider tires can run lower pressure.
tireWidth.adjustment: 26 x 2.0 MTB: 30-50 psi; hooked 700 x 25C road: 90-110 psi. Hookless systems remain capped at 73 psi / 5.0 bar.

terrain.explanation: Soft or muddy terrain needs lower pressure for grip; rocky terrain needs higher pressure for rim protection.

ridingStyle.explanation: Aggressive racing needs higher pressure; casual riding can use lower pressure.
ridingStyle.adjustment: Hooked racing: 110-130 psi; leisure: 80-100 psi. These higher ranges do not apply to hookless systems.

rimDesign.explanation: Wider rims support lower pressure; narrow rims require higher pressure.

typical.title: 3. Typical pressure ranges (approximate)
typical.road: Hooked road bikes: 80-120 psi, up to 130 psi for racing; hookless road systems: never over 73 psi / 5.0 bar.
typical.mountain: Mountain bikes: 30-60 psi, with XC often at 25-40 psi.

tips.title: 4. Practical tips
tips.sidewall: Check the sidewall and follow the manufacturer's recommended range.
tips.gauge: Use a reliable gauge instead of relying on feel.
tips.inspect: Inspect regularly because tires lose air naturally; check weekly or before rides.
tips.extremes: Avoid extremes: never exceed the maximum or drop below the minimum pressure.
tips.seasonal: Adjust seasonally because cold weather can lower pressure by around 10%.

warnings.title: 5. Risks & warnings
warnings.high: Too high: harsh ride and potential rim damage.
warnings.low: Too low: pinch flats and poor handling.
warnings.neglect: Neglecting checks: gradual air loss reduces performance and safety.
warnings.hookless: Hookless safety red line: never exceed 73 PSI / 5.0 bar, even if the tire is marked for a higher pressure.
